outline: Bioenergy is referred to the energy stored in living or recently living biological organisms, such as animals, plants and microbes. The source of bioenergy can be traced back from plants harvesting the sunlight and converting it to glucose, then to other biopolymers such as polysaccharides. The technologies for developing bioenergy, with an emphasis on environmentally compatible, consist of gene cloning technology from molecular biology and enzymatic control and catalytic chemistry (i.e. green chemistry).  The course is an introduction course on the types of polysaccharides in animals and plants, how scientist use system biology to develop bioengergy.

flexible_learning.content: During Weeks 17 and 18, students will conduct independent literature research on cutting-edge developments in bioenergy, biomass conversion technologies, and net-zero carbon strategies. In Week 17, student will synthesize relevant peer-reviewed journal articles and finalize their project topics. In Week 18, each group will deliver their final oral presentations and submit a comprehensive written report demonstrating their analytical understanding of bioenergy systems and sustainability.
flexible_learning.outcome: Assessment is conducted through a final oral group presentation and a written literature review report. Evaluation criteria include technical comprehension of bioenergy principles, critical analysis of selected literature, clarity of presentation slides, and effective teamwork and Q&A interaction.

assessment: Evaluation: Class participation (40%), Midterm report (30%), Final report (30%)
